newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa up, Sept clears 1,150 in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa up, Sept clears 1,150 in brisk trade.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures clinched slight gains by the close on Monday in brisk trade with September clearing the previous hurdle at 1,150 stg -- the top seen in the previous three consecutive sessions.

Traders said the heavy volume of 14,112 lots was inflated by crosses, AA trades and switches as operators squared their books at the end of the July/June financial year and ahead of July's first tender tender on Tuesday.
Second-month July led actives with 8,111 lots traded.
"People were tidying up their positions at the end of the month and with July becoming tenderable from tomorrow," said one trader.
July open positions remained large, standing at 15,065 lots on Friday, two days before the first tender day.

July and September were seven stg up each at 1,131 and 1,151 a tonne respectively at the close. September peaked at 1,150 stg for the past three sessions in a row. But it still faced a tough resistance at the June 24 high of 1,162.
Traders said while the overall bullish sentiment remained intact, today's direction was merely following which ever way the spot July moved.
But sellers were scarce with the market trading just about 20 stg away from its recent highs.
They were also cautious over the weather in Ivory Coast, which is experiencing the wettest June since 1982.

Fundamentally, traders were keeping an eye on second quarter Euripean cocoa grind data, due later this week or early next week. Analyts said the figures were expected to show a mixed trend. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
